relevance_rank_note: Repeats the ApoE3-vs-ApoE4 surface biotinylation assay in primary neurons and shows genetic NHE6 (Slc9a6) deletion removes the ApoE4-induced loss of receptor surface expression; the rest of the paper is plaque load and synaptic plasticity, which does not bear on receptor recycling.

description: In wildtype (Slc9a6+) primary neurons treated with Reelin, ApoE4-conditioned medium reduced Apoer2 surface/total levels far more than ApoE3, and in Slc9a6- (NHE6 knockout) littermate neurons the ApoE4-induced reduction was gone, so genetic loss of NHE6 fully reverses the ApoE4 recycling block. Effect and stars are ApoE4 vs no-ApoE control in Slc9a6+ neurons, not a direct ApoE4 vs ApoE3 test.
quote: Apoer2 recycling was completely restored in Slc9a6- neurons treated with ApoE4 (Figure 4C).
summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (less surface Apoer2); (ApoE4 + NHE6 knockout) -> (surface Apoer2 restored to control)
system: Primary cortical neurons from wildtype (Slc9a6+) and germline NHE6-knockout (Slc9a6-) mouse littermate embryos, E18, DIV10-14; 30 min 5 ug/ml HEK293-secreted human ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned medium, then 2 ug/ml Reelin 30 min; cell surface biotinylation, surface/total Apoer2 immunoblot. Deviation: mouse primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE and a knockout gene background, not non-aged non-AD human brain cells, and neurons rather than astrocytes.
human_check: eff is the ApoE4 bar (~27) against the no-ApoE control bar (~100) in the Slc9a6+ half of Fig 4C; the authors print no percentage. The *** bracket in Fig 4C runs from the Slc9a6+ control bar to the Slc9a6+ ApoE4 bar; legend key is *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.005.

description: The same assay read out for glutamate receptor subunits showed ApoE4 reduced surface GluN2B, GluA1 and GluA2/3 in wildtype neurons (ApoE3 producing a smaller reduction), and NHE6 knockout restored all three to control levels. Effect and stars are ApoE4 vs no-ApoE control in Slc9a6+ neurons, not a direct ApoE4 vs ApoE3 test.
quote: In addition, genetic loss of NHE6 equally restored the ApoE4-impaired surface expression of AMPA and NMDA receptor subunits (Figure 4D–F).
summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (less surface GluN2B, GluA1, GluA2/3); (ApoE4 + NHE6 knockout) -> (surface levels restored)
system: Primary cortical neurons from wildtype and Slc9a6- (NHE6 knockout) mouse littermate embryos, E18, DIV10-14; 5 ug/ml ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned medium 30 min then 2 ug/ml Reelin 30 min; surface biotinylation, surface/total immunoblot of GluN2B, GluA1, GluA2/3. Deviation: mouse primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE and a knockout gene background, not non-aged non-AD human brain cells.
human_check: Three receptors are pooled in one row, so no single effect size applies (Slc9a6+ ApoE4 bars read ~26 GluN2B, ~35 GluA1, ~29 GluA2/3 of a 100 control). The P code is the *** bracket on the control-vs-ApoE4 comparison in each of panels D-F; the ApoE3 bars in D-F carry a separate * (p < 0.05).

description: ApoE3 itself produced a small but reproducible reduction of Apoer2 surface levels relative to no-ApoE control, and this smaller ApoE3 effect was also abolished in NHE6-knockout neurons, indicating a graded, pH-dependent effect rather than an ApoE4-only phenomenon.
quote: We previously reported that the addition of ApoE3 to neurons also affects Apoer2 trafficking to a small, but reproducible extent. This was also abolished in Slc9a6- neurons (Figure 4C).
summary: (no ApoE -> ApoE3) -> (slightly less surface Apoer2, much less than ApoE4); (ApoE3 + NHE6 knockout) -> (restored)
system: Primary cortical neurons from wildtype and Slc9a6- mouse littermate embryos, E18, DIV10-14; 5 ug/ml ApoE3 conditioned medium 30 min then 2 ug/ml Reelin 30 min; surface biotinylation of Apoer2. Deviation: mouse primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE, not non-aged non-AD human brain cells.
location: Fig 4C (Slc9a6+ E3+R bar vs C+R bar)
human_check: eff is the Slc9a6+ ApoE3 bar (~77) against the control bar (~100) in Fig 4C, read off the figure. No star appears on the ApoE3 bar in panel C (unlike panels D-F, where ApoE3 carries *), so no P value can be assigned to this ApoE3 contrast; the text calls the effect 'small, but reproducible' without statistics.
